sentences.text: The brief facts of the case of the prosecution are that the accused NO.1 is the husband of Cw 1 and they got married at Bhadravathi in the year 2001.
The accused looked after CW 1 very well for 6 months and later when she gave birth to a female child, the accused used to abuse her for giving birth to a girl child and used to harass her mentally.
In the year 2008 Cw 1 again gave birth to a girl child , hence, the accused used to pick up quarrel very often and also abused her for giving birth to girl child.

The accused sold the property without knowledge of Cw 1 and  3 CC.No.5254/16 when she asked him why he had sold the property, he picked quarrel with Cw 1 and also did not take care of the family, hence, her parents took care of her.
Later when the accused wanted to sell the property which he had inherited by way of gift deed, CW 1 filed objection with the BBMP authority.
Hence, the accused No.1 abused Cw 1 in filthy language.

3. It has further alleged that on 24.10.14 the accused has destroyed all the phots and threatened Cw 1 with dire consequences of life if she does not go out of the house and also affixed threatening letter to the door.
The accused also harassed Cw1 to bring dowry from her parental house.

That on 11.11.2014 when Cw 1 was going with her mother,
the accused all of a sudden restrained her movement and abused her in filthy language and slapped CW 1 with his hands in the public place and also threatened Cw 1 with dire consequences of life if she did not vacate the house and thereby committed an offence u/s. 341, 323, 504, 506 498A of IPC.
4. On the basis of the complaint of the CW 1, this crime has been registered by Yeshwanthapura Police Station.
During the crime stage, the accused produced before the court and remanded to JC.
Later on accused hs represented through counsel and filed bail application and enlarged on  4 CC.No.5254/16 bail.

After investigation, Investigating officer filed the charge Shobha vs Ravikumar on 12 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/149649977/

sentences.text: The cognizance for the said offences are taken.
5. The copies of the prosecution papers have furnished to the accused as contemplated u/s.207 of Cr.P.C.,

After being heard the arguments before charge, as there were no grounds to discharge the accused , charge for the alleged offences have been framed & read over,
explained to the accused in the language best known to him The accused has not pleaded guilty and claims to be tried.

Hence, the case taken up for trial.
 6.
In order to prove the guilt of the accused prosecution has examined the complainant as PW 1 out of 10 witnesses as cited in the chargesheet.
3 documents have been marked as Ex.P.1 to 3.
Since the PW 1 being the victim/complainant has turned hostile and there is no incriminating evidence against the accused , examination of accused u/s.313 of Cr.P.C., has been dispensed with.
Heard the arguments of learned APP and counsel for accused persons.
Perused.

On the basis of the above, the following points have arises for my consideration : -
 1) Whether prosecution proves beyond  reasonable doubt that CW1 and  accused got married at Bhadravathi in  the year 2001 and when she gave birth  to a female child, the accused abused  her for giving birth to a girl child and  harassed her mentally and  subsequently in the year 2008 when Cw  1 again gave birth to a girl child the  accused pick up quarrel abused her for  giving birth to girl child and harassed  Cw 1 mentally and on 24.10.14 he

abused and threatened her to go out of  the house otherwise threatened to kill  her and on 11.11.14 the accused has  abused her in public road and  demanded to bring dowry from parental  house and subjected her to cruelty and

thereby committed an offence u/s.498A  of IPC?

3  2) Whether prosecution proves beyond  reasonable doubt that in furtherance of  act, the accused sold the property and

when Cw 1 questioned him, the accused  abused Cw 1 in filthy language and  again when she was going with her  mother he abused Cw 1 in filthy  wordings in public road knowing fully  well that it will provoke public peace of  Cw 1 and thereby committed an  offence punishable u/s.504 of IPC?

3) Whether prosecution proves beyond  reasonable doubt that in furtherance of  above act, that on 11.11.2014 when Cw  1 was proceeding along with her mother,
 the accused all of a sudden picked up  quarrel with Cw1 and restrained her  movement and thereby committed an  offence punishable u/s.341 of IPC?
 4) Whether prosecution proves beyond  reasonable doubt that in furtherance of  above act, the accused restrained  movement of Cw1, picked up quarrel  and slapped CW 1 with his hands in  the public place and caused simple  hurt and thereby committed an offence  punishable u/s.323 of IPC?
 5) Whether prosecution proves beyond  reasonable doubt that in furtherance of  above act, the accused threatened Cw  1 with dire consequence of life if she did  not vacate the house and thereby  committed an offence u/s.506 of IPC ?
 6) What order?
 8. My answer to the above points is as under;
 Point No.1 to 5- In the Negative  Point No.6-As per final order for the following :
 REASONS

9 . Point No.1 to 5: Since all these points are interlinked  7 CC.No.5254/16 with each other, I have taken them together for common Shobha vs Ravikumar on 12 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/149649977/
4 discussion in order to avoid the repetition.

According to the prosecution, accused has committed the offences u/s.341,
323, 504, 506 and 498A of IPC.
In order to prove the guilt of the accused , the prosecution has examined the complainant as PW.1.
The PW 1 has deposed that she and accused got married on 12.12.2001 at Bhadravathi and they have two children.
The accused never abused her and assaulted her nor harassed her for dowry.
About 2 years ago back, when she went to police station, they have took the signature on two documents which are the complaint and mahazar and they have marked as Ex.P.1 & 2.
She has deposed that she does not know what has written in Ex.P.1 & 2.
Thus she has totally turned hostile to the case of the prosecution.
10. At request of learned senior APP this witness has been treated as hostile witness and permission was accorded to cross examine her.
In the cross examination the learned Sr.APP suggested the case of the prosecution and same has been denied by the witness.
On the basis of the above evidence of PW.1 the court cannot come to conclusion that the accused has committed the offence as alleged by the prosecution.
If really there was any incident, definitely the PW.1 should have given evidence on par with the avernments made in the complaint.
Here the PW.1 turned hostile, in the  8 CC.No.5254/16 cross examination she has categorically admitted that, she and accused have compromised the matter.
That is the reason why PW.1 has not given any evidence supporting the case of the prosecution.
In a criminal justice system, if a tiny doubt arises in the mind of the court, benefit of doubt shall be extended to the accused persons.

In this case, not only tiny doubt but the strong doubt arise in the mind of the court,
because the victim herself has not supported the case of the prosecution.
Hence, the prosecution has utterly failed to prove the guilt of the accused beyond all reasonable doubt.
Hence, in my opinion it is a fit case to extend benefit of doubt to the accused .
Accordingly point Nos 1 to 5 are answered in the Negative.
11 . POINT NO.6

: For the aforesaid reason and discussion, I proceed to pass the following:
 ORDER Acting under section 248(1) of Cr.P.C. Accused is hereby acquitted for the offences punishable U/s.341, 323, 504, 506, 498A of IPC .
The bail bond executed by the accused stands cancelled.
However, Accused shall execute personal bond of Rs.50,000/- by undertaking to appear before the Honble appellate Court, if any appeal is filed.

It is not a fit case to award victim compensation as provided U/s.357(1) of Cr.P.C., (Dictated to Shobha vs Ravikumar on 12 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/149649977/
